newsitem.title: UK: EIU sees Ivory cocoa crop at 980,000 T in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: EIU sees Ivory cocoa crop at 980,000 T in 1996/97.

text.p: The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) has forecast the Ivorian cocoa crop at 980,000 tonnes in the current 1996/97 season, down from an estimated 1.2 million in 1995/96.

In its latest quarterly report, the EIU put the total production at 2.6 million tonnes, down from 2.848 million, resulting in a supply deficit of 145,000 tonnes after a surplus of 133,000 tonnes last season.
"We have lowered our 1996/97 production forecast following evidence (not yet conclusive) that West African crops may not be as good as previously projected," it said.
"It includes lower reported purchases from farmers and arrivals at ports, and low rainfall in some areas may have hampered mid-crop development," it added.
The EIU pegged Indonesian production at a new record of 325,000 tonnes but added that the growth was slowing.
Malaysia was seen producing 10,000 tonnes more than last season at 120,000 tonnes while Brazil was seen slightly lower at 225,000.

Looking further ahead, the EIU said Ivorian output was unlikely to equal the record harvest of 1995/96 but Ghana had the potential to lift output back to 400,000 tonnes, from 350,000 tonnes it forecast for this season.
It expected prices to rise more steeply than previously estimated as a result of bigger production shortfalls.
